text: What is the primary purpose of a Constructor in Java?
explanation: Constructor is a special kind of method mainly designed to perform initializing actions when a new object is created.

text: Which of the following is TRUE about a Constructor's name?
choices: It must have the same name as the class
It must start with a lowercase letter
explanation: Constructors differs from general methods in that a Constructor must have the same name as the class name.

text: What is the return type of a Constructor?
choices: It does not have a return type
explanation: Constructors do not have a return type, not even void.

text: How is a constructor invoked?
choices: Implicitly when an object is constructed using 'new'
Automatically when the class is compiled
explanation: Constructor is invoked implicitly only when an object is constructed using the new operator. It cannot be invoked explicitly elsewhere.

text: What feature allows multiple methods to have the same name but different signatures?
explanation: Having different methods that have the same name but a different signature is called 'method overloading' or polymorphism.

text: Which visibility modifier provides the 'widest' access?
explanation: Public provides the widest visibility. Any method or variable is visible to the class in which it is defined and to all classes outside.

text: What is the default access modifier if no keyword is used?
explanation: If no modifier is used, it is the default one having visibility only within a package that contains the class. This is known as 'package' protection.

text: Which visibility level is restricted to only the class where it is defined?
explanation: Private provides the narrowest visibility. The private methods and variables are directly accessible only by the methods defined within a class.

text: What happens if you define a parameterized constructor but no no-argument constructor?
choices: The default constructor is still available
The default constructor is no more available
explanation: In presence of user-defined constructors in a class, the default constructor is no more available. If needed, we must provide it explicitly.

text: Which protection level is used to allow access to subclasses or 'friend' methods?
explanation: Protected protection is used to allow the access only to subclasses or to share with the methods declared as 'friend' (in concept).

text: What is Data Encapsulation best achieved by?
choices: Making as much data as private as possible
explanation: The best way to provide data encapsulation is to make as much data as private as possible, separating design from implementation.

text: If a variable 'length' is private in class 'Rectangle', how can another class access it?
choices: Through public getter methods like getLength()
explanation: It can be made available indirectly by the methods that are accessible by another class (e.g., getLength() and getWidth()).

text: Polymorphism means:
explanation: Polymorphism means 'many forms'. It allows different methods to have the same name.

text: Can constructors be overloaded?
choices: Yes, by varying the parameter list
Only if they have different names
explanation: Like other methods, constructors can also be overloaded. It is possible with varying list of parameters.

text: What is a 'Default Constructor'?
explanation: Every class is having its default constructor; sometimes referred to as no-argument constructor.

text: Which modifier provides visibility to classes defined in other packages?
explanation: Public provides visibility to classes defined in other package also. To provide public access, use access modifier public.

text: When is the default constructor NOT generated automatically?
choices: When the class has no variables
When a user-defined constructor is present
explanation: In presence of user-defined constructors in a class, default constructor is no more available.

text: Method signatures include:
explanation: The method's signature is a combination of the method name and the list of parameters.

text: What is the visibility of a variable declared without any modifier?
explanation: This is the next level of access that has no precise name... declared as 'friend'. It is the default level of protection (package).

text: Which statement correctly calls a user-defined no-argument constructor?
explanation: To solve the error, add user-defined no-argument constructor 'Room() {}' and execute... Room r3 = new Room();.

text: Why do we use private variables?
choices: To hide data from the world's sight (Encapsulation)
explanation: This provides data encapsulation; hiding data from the world's sight and limiting its manipulation.

text: In `printline(int n, char ch)`, what makes it different from `printline(int n)`?
explanation: It uses polymorphism to print a line as per specified parameters (different signature).

text: Which access modifier is considered the 'narrowest'?
explanation: Table 8.1 shows private has the narrowest visibility.

text: If `rect1` is an object of `Rectangle` with private `length`, does `rect1.length = 10` work?
explanation: Note the error in the output pane that says 'length has private access in Rectangle'. This means it is not accessible directly.

text: A package statement is used to:
explanation: Package is used to organize classes. Package statement should be added as the first non-comment line.

text: Which of these is NOT one of the 'Four P's of Protection'?
explanation: The Four P's of Protection are public, package (default), protected, and private.

text: What is the syntax for a constructor of class `Room`?
explanation: A constructor has the same name as the class and no return type. Example: `Room(float l, float w) ...`.

text: Access modifiers are also known as:
explanation: Access control is about controlling visibility. So, access modifiers are also known as visibility modifiers.

text: Can a constructor initialize attributes with different values than the default?
explanation: We may write our own constructors to initialize the attributes of 'Room' object with different parameters.

text: The scope of a private variable is:
choices: Only the class it is defined in
explanation: The private methods and variables are directly accessible only by the methods defined within a class. They cannot be seen by any other class.
